cases.title: Rebooting Secondary GV caused both Primary & Secondary to go Out of Service following Secondary GV boot up - TIBU-18930
cases.section_path: Previous TIBU scenarios
cases.custom_steps:
Rebooting Secondary GV caused both Primary & Secondary to go Out of Service following Secondary GV boot up. 

Tayo observed this issue initially in QA testing, here is comment that he provided on TIBU-18310:

This happens when the secondary device is rebooted via CF Remote commands
Initially it looked like the audit spamming issue had returned, as after the reboot I logged into the primary device as a Technician and the pending audits showed “101”.
Upon trying to reproduce this I am unable to confirm the number of audits as the primary device becomes unresponsive to tech cards, I can confirm though that this scenario causes the Device Status for the primary to spam again (although not to the extent shown originally in this ticket)

In my instance I did not observe any audit spam produced by either device, however I was also unable to log into Technician on the Primary GV as the Technician card was not being read by the Validator.

Expected Result:

Both GV will be In Service following Secondary GV reboot and set to the mode they were previously set to before the reboot occurred 

Actual Result:

Both GV are Out of Service following Secondary GV reboot

Primary GV Logs:

Open Primary GV Logs.zip

cases.title: Changing location of Both GVs resulted in both being out Of Service - TIBU-18941
cases.section_path: Previous TIBU scenarios

cases.title: TIBU-14711: TL GV Primary & Secondary State Issues
cases.section_path: Fixes/Changes / 4.1.0.21969
cases.custom_steps:
Description

Build: 1.0.304.17886

Scenarios tested on real devices with Simulated Gate

Both GVs set to OOS, secondary rebooted - PASS

Primary and Secondary set to Out of Service using CF command

Secondary rebooted

Primary & Secondary remained OOS as expected

Both GVs set to OOS, primary rebooted - FAIL

Primary and Secondary set to Out of Service using CF command

Primary rebooted

Secondary went into ‘No Entry’ mode while the Primary was rebooting and returned to OOS once the Primary was back up. Primary returned to OOS as expected.

GVs set to Emergency Open, Primary rebooted - PASS

Emergency open sent to both using CF command

Primary rebooted

Secondary remained in 'Emergency Open' as expected, and primary returned to 'No Entry.

GVs set to Emergency Open, Secondary rebooted - FAIL

Emergency open sent to both using CF command

Secondary rebooted

Primary returned to ‘Present Card…’, Secondary returned to ‘No Entry’

Furthermore, when tested using a real Primary and simulated Secondary, if we simulate a ‘Register secondary’ to the primary when the primary has been put into OOS or ‘Emergency Open', the primary remains in the state issued via command. However, if the Primary is rebooted after the command and receives another registration from the Secondary it will return to 'Present Card…’ screen.

the order in which the devices are rebooted following the command being issued seems to impact the behavior.

When in Emergency Open if the Primary is rebooted, and then the Secondary is rebooted, the Primary will return to ‘Present Card…’ and the Secondary to ‘No Entry’.

If instead, after the command is issued, and only the secondary is rebooted, the Primary remains on ‘No Entry’ but the secondary also displays ‘No Entry’.

Logs for scenarios 1-4 are attached.

cases.title: TIBU-14722: TL GV - Tech Sign Off on Secondary GV Leaves Gate In Maintenance Mode

cases.custom_steps:
Description

Technician Sign-Off after Sign-On to Secondary GV leaves the Gate in Maintenance mode and results in the GVs either showing OOS, or one showing OOS and the other showing No Entry.

Steps to Reproduce

Ensure the Gate is operational - the Primary is showing Present Card screen, secondary showing No Entry

Present a technician Card to the Secondary GV

Proceed to Sign in as a valid technician - Both GVs go OOS as expected

Once signed on, sign off again

Expected Result

Primary returns to the Present Card screen

Secondary returns to No Entry screen

Actual Result

Primary displays OOS or No Entry

Secondary displays OOS or No Entry

cases.custom_steps:
Description

GV issues following Emergency Switch testing. Gates displayed strange behaviour with Gate paddles opening and closing and both heads sporadically flicking between different modes followed by eventually going OOS and could not be restored. Please see audit trail below:

10:25 - signed in and out as technician on primary head, GV rebooted itself. When it booted back up it remained OOS

10:27- signed in and out of technician mode on secondary head, flashed up "Emergency Exit" then back OOS. At 10:32, the secondary head came back and displayed "Emergency Exit"

10:35 - flicked emergency exit switch to try and bring it out of Emergency Mode, secondary head went to OOS and primary head remained OOS. Gate paddles opened correctly

10:36 - Reset emergency exit button, paddles remained to OOS. Signed in and out of technician mode, Primary head displayed No Entry briefly then Gate paddles opened and closed twice before returning to normal OOS mode.

10:39 - same process as above. Hit emergency switch, Gates opened with primary head displaying No Entry briefly, secondary flicked up with Emergency Mode then OOS. Reset switch and Gates returned to closed position. Signed in and out as tech on primary head. Gate paddles went through open and close motion again.

10:42 - Emergency exit again to try and bring both GV heads back into Service as Station Manager shows Emergency Mode status. This time signed into Tech mode on secondary head. Showed "Card still present", then went back to Emergency Exit on secondary head.

10:45 – Powered off Gates and left them off power for 15 minutes to see if discharging the caps would help.

11:00 – Restored power to GV but both heads remained OOS when booted back up

11:19 – Changed location of both heads to York Street to see if a location change and automatic reboot would bring them back in service but this did not work.

11:38 - Power cycled Gates and when they came back, secondary head was showing "Please Proceed" like it was in Fully Free mode. Sent it Entry and Exit command which brought secondary head in but validation failed to open Gate paddles

The Gates have been out of service since we started testing Emergency and Fully Free mode yesterday so not sure if that’s also a cause of the problems.

cases.title: TIBU-18302 - Reboot command puts primary device OOS temporarily
cases.section_path: Fixes/Changes / 4.1.2
cases.custom_steps:
build : 5.99.9999.19563

Sending a ‘reboot’  remote command from Cloudflare- Asset manager puts the primary GV out of service

 STR:

Go to cloudfare -Asset manager

Select the device by it ID

On the remote commands dropdown- select reboot

09-04 14:02:11:051211 [I] Transaction      [  53] NotificationRunner - finished rule 'BRRemoteCommand' with status 'Failed'.  Queue is Not Paused
09-04 14:02:11:051394 [I] Transaction      [  53] NotificationRunner - starting rule 'BRProcessStateNotification'
09-04 14:02:11:051579 [I] Transaction      [  55] Moved to state: ErrorOutOfService

We have the GV configured in “INTEGRATION” mode, which means when the GV boots up we see the 4 buttons at the top of the screen (“Customer”, “Maintenance”, “State”, “Reboot”). The “Reboot” option from this screen does not work (Permission Denial)

If however from the menu I press the “Maintenance” instead of “Reboot”, and then from the Maintenance app go to System->Reboot then the GV does reboot

If we allow the application to boot, and then try and perform a remote reboot command from CloudFare, then the reboot does not work (Permission Denial)

The above would indicate that the hardware itself is all OK, and that it is capable of rebooting.

To further confuse the situation:

If I take the microSD card from our other GV, which does respond to the reboot commands, and put it into the GV that we have problems with, then with this microSD card the GV will reboot correctly when the “Reboot” button seen during botting is pressed, and will also respond to reboot commands sent from CloudFare when the application is allowed to load

The thing is, both microSD cards were created in exactly the same way, installed with exactly the same software

There were some thoughts that it could be the STM32 firmware, or it could be the SDK version declared in the manifest but we have not conclusively proved this one way or the other.

Done

cases.title: TIBU-21005: TL GV : Regression in barcode throughput performance
cases.section_path: Fixes/Changes / 4.1.5
cases.custom_steps:
Description

During Translink’s testing, they have found that the throughput of barcode validations has regressed/become quite a bit slower than in previous builds and they see this as a blocker for the rollout of 4.1.4. Unfortunately this means we will need to look at addressing this.

The primary cause appears to be because we intermittently can no longer present a barcode for validation whilst the “Barcode Success” green screen is being shown from a previous barcode validation. The barcode is successfully scanned on the barcode reader, but is ignored by the application. This means we need to wait for the “Barcode Success” screen to close down before presenting another barcode which slows down the throughput.

A fix is required that allows us to reliably present further barcodes for validation whilst the “Barcode Success” green screen is being displayed for previous barcode valdations.

Environment


None
Closure Reason


None
Requirements


GIVEN A successful barcode validation has been performed
AND The GV is displaying the green "Barcode Success" validation screen
WHEN Another barcode is presented for validation
THEN The barcode should be successfully validated and allow the passenger to pass through the gate

GIVEN A successful barcode validation has been performed
AND The GV is displaying the green "Barcode Success" validation screen
WHEN Another barcode is presented for validation
THEN Then the green "Barcode Success" screen should remain displayed
AND The timeout of the green "Barcode Success" screen should be reset (so that the screen does not timeout before the specified timeout time)

cases.title: TIBU-22674: TL GV - Barcode Reader Dropout Possible Link to ABT enabled in error
cases.section_path: Fixes/Changes / 4.2.0
cases.custom_steps:
Description

Although the latest 4.1.5 GV software is proving much improved at dealing with barcode reader dropouts and recovering automatically, there are still some instances where the barcode reader drops out and does not recover. Additionally, Translink are still very, very keen on getting to the bottom of why the barcode readers are dropping out in the first place.

Whilst looking into logs for an unrelated reason, there appears to be the following logged at exactly the time the barcode reader is dropping out:

04-24 10:02:13:873047 [I] Abt              [  54] [AbtWrapper.Enable] on entry set to [TapDisabled]

I have checked this on two different GV heads, and it is consistent. The above log message is logged, and only logged, at the same time that barcode readers drop out. We then appear to get a number of TapEnabled messages afterwards:

04-24 10:02:14:124924 [I] Abt              [  60] [AbtWrapper.Enable] on entry set to [TapEnabled]

Logs for head 000045 and 000065 attached.

000065 had a flurry of barcode reader dropouts at 10:02 on the 24th April.
000045 had a flurry of barcode reader dropouts at 10:02 and at 11:08 on the 24th April.

In all these cases, the TapDisabled message was logged.

On GVs we are not configured/should not be configured to support open payment taps, and so we should not be seeing the TapDisabled (or TapEnabled) messages at all.

This needs investigating:

Is this the cause of barcode reader dropouts or a side effect/symptom

Both the FEIG reader and Barcode reader are powered by USB, does Enabling/Disabling taps draw additional power at all that could brown out the barcode reader

Why are we seeing TapDisabled/TapEnabled messages at all when the GVs are not/should not be configured to deal with ABT

cases.title: TIBU-22904: TL GV - Improve Logging to reduce noise and to help better identify ongoing issues in live
cases.section_path: Fixes/Changes / 4.2.0
cases.custom_steps:
Description

Background:

There are a number of ongoing issues being reported on the live gates, some examples are:

1) Barcode reader dropouts still being reported : the majority (95-98%) of these do recover automatically and last < 10 seconds however a small (2-5%) do not recover and require a head reboot. Unclear from the logs why on some occassions the barcode reader does not recover. T

he barcode reader seems to be totally AWOL and does not illuminate the LEDs when a barcode is waved in front of it. In the past (4.0.5 build, which did not include barcode recovery code) when a barcode reader dropped out, then it would still illuminate the LEDs when a barcode is waved in front of it.

2) GVs can go OOS. This can be a temporary scenario, for example a head may go OOS for 30 seconds and then automatically go back into service, or it could be a permanent issue where the head goes OOS and requires a reboot to recover. Importantly, in the more permanent cases it does appear that in the vast number of cases, a head (remote CF) reboot does recover the issue which suggests that this is an application issue.

3) GVs can “randomly” perform a paddle calibration. This is usually both paddles, but we have seen on occassion that only 1 paddle will go through the calibration. This is expected to be a GoEasier gate issue, but we need to look at logging to see if we can confidently show it is a GoEasier issue (and not an effect of our gate heads “confusing” the GoEasier interface such as, for example, both the primary and secondary heads sending a message to the GoEasier interface at the same time).

The above scenarios are difficult to get to the bottom of because we are unable to reproduce them on our test gates, and the logging is not “sufficient” to be able to identify the root cause of the problems.

This is further compounded by the fact that the application logs are very “noisy” which (too) frequent requests to obtain the FEIG manifest (appears every 5 seconds) which means the log files are not only noisy, but also only log around 36 hours of activity because they are quickly filled up. An example log file is attached showing how noisy it is with the FEIG manifest requests.

Task Aims:

1. We want to “improve” the logging, by reducing the noise that is generated due to the FEIG manifest request. It is hoped that this is due to some poor configuration and that we should be able to greatly reduce the frequency in the configuration for how often the FEIG manifest is requested. Note that currently there are absolutely no datasets created or distributed for the FEIG on the Gates and so we could reduce the freuquency to every 24 hours without any negative impact.

2. We want to consider what additional logging could be added that would be beneficial to the ongoing barcode reader issues being reported. For example the fact that the barcode reader does not respond to barcodes being waved in front of it suggests that we may be actively turning the barcode reader off, or not starting the hunt for barcodes again. Do we have sufficient logging around the commands that we sent to the barcode reader such that we can see in the logs if/when we configure the barcode reader and/or when we enable/disable it?

3. We want to consider what additional logging can be added to better help identify why the gates are going OOS, both temporarily and when more permanently. Does this point to a remaining issue with the state engine logic, or is it because we are getting a status message back from the GoEasier interface that triggers the application to go OOS? We need to look at improving the logging around what decisions are being made by the gates when it goes OOS so we can better identify the root causes. Can we also consider what if any additional messages we can log based on status messages back from the GoEasier interface, whether this would be logging existing status messages we get back from the GoEasier interface, or making additional queries to the GoEasier interface to obtain more information back which may be useful for ongoing investigations (note that we talk through the OS/platform rather than directly with the GoEasier interface so this may require OS/Platform support).

Timescales:

It is anticipated that the improved logging will be a “stepping stone” to help us identify these issues to either:

a. Fix in code
b. Engage with GoEasier if we identify an issue with their interface

We therefore want to look at improving the logging for the next (4.1.6) GV build and so although this may appear to be low priority as it does not add any actual fixes, it is actually fairly critical to the ability to understand the remaining issues and gives us a better chance of fixing them in the proceeding (4.1.7+) GV builds and thus needs to be looked at with high priority.



Environment


None
Acceptance Criteria


None
Closure Reason


None
Requirements


GIVEN An issue is reported on a live GV
WHEN I obtain logs remotely
THEN I want to be able to obtain at a minimum 3 full days of application log information

GIVEN An issue is reported on a live GV
WHEN I obtain logs for investigation
THEN The logs need to be sufficient for helping investigate the underlying issue reported
Attachments
1

cases.title: TIBU-23837
cases.section_path: Fixes/Changes / 4.2.0
cases.custom_steps:
Description

Translink have reported that an Irish Rail barcode when presented to the GVs will cause the barcode reader to dropout. Typically the barcode reader will recover after the dropout, but they have had two occasions when the barcode reader has dropped out and not recovered until a power cycle.

Irish Rail barcodes are not meant to be supported on the gates. What we should expect to see when they are scanned is the red error screen “Barcode Type Invalid” and indeed when these same Irish Rail barcodes are scanned on a PV or a HHD this is what we do see (the “Barcode Type Invalid” error screen). 

Please see attached a PDF of numerous Irish Rail barcodes that can be used to reproduce this issue. NOTE That when the PDF is physically printed, the barcode fails to scan : it is a very dense barcode. The best way to use them is to zoom into the barcode in the PDF, take a photo of the barcode with your phone and then present the photo on your phone to the barcode reader.

The result is a little mixed:

You will see that the LED bar on the top of the GV head will flicker a bit, and then the amber “Barcodes Not Available” banner will be shown, however this may require a few presentations of the barcode before the amber banner is shown. We have not seen any occasions where the correct behavior is observed (i.e the red “Barcode Type Invalid” error screen). 

Steps to Reproduce:

Open PDF, zoom into barcode on PDF and take a photo of the barcode with your phone

Present the photo of the barcode taken on your phone to the GV barcode reader

Expected Result:

The barcode reader should scan the barcode, and then the GV should show the red “Barcode Type Invalid” error screen

Actual Result:

The barcode appears to scan successfully, however the GV LED bar at the top flickers, and the amber “Barcodes Not Available” banner is shown



Environment


None
Closure Reason


None
Requirements


GIVEN I have an Irish Rail Barcode
WHEN The barcode is presented to the GV barcode reader
THEN The GV should show the "Barcode Type Invalid" error message

GIVEN I have an Irish Rail Barcode
WHEN The barcode is presented to the GV barcode reader
THEN The barcode reader should not drop out
AND The GV should not show the amber "Barcodes Not Available" bar
